description: Evidence to Knowledge conversion, interpretation error, and confidence calibration. Values are initial candidates, not balanced.

estimate.note: Every knowledge record is a range plus a confidence. Width comes from how much is known; offset comes from who interpreted it.
estimate.note_min_width: Never collapses to a point. Even a long-managed fighter keeps a small band.

width_drivers.note_halving: Each N independent pieces of evidence roughly halves the remaining excess width above min_width.
width_drivers.note_contradiction: Conflicting evidence widens the range rather than flipping the estimate. Belief should not oscillate.

bias.note: Interpretation error is systematic, not random noise. A weak interpreter is wrong in predictable directions.
bias.note_sources: Each source has a direction. Beating weak opposition inflates; winning on a favourable style matchup reads as raw ability; visible physical traits are over-weighted against technique.

freshness.note: Stale knowledge widens and stays anchored to the past. A fighter who grew since observation is misjudged low, not merely unknown.

confidence.note: Confidence is what the interpreter believes, not how right they are. A weak interpreter can be narrow and wrong.
confidence.note_overconfidence: Low-skill interpreters report higher confidence than their accuracy justifies. This is what makes a bad scout dangerous rather than merely useless.

domain_difficulty.note: Multiplier on width. Some things are simply harder to read from outside.

potential.note: Never exposed as a ceiling number. Breakthrough capacity is not estimable at all.
